Backends

Choose and configure filesystem backends for deep agents. You can specify routes to different backends, implement virtual filesystems, and enforce policies.

graph TD %% Main Header FT[Filesystem Tools] --> Backend[Backend] %% Middleware/Logic Layer Backend --> Custom[Custom] Backend --> Composite[Composite] %% Direct connections to bottom layer Backend --> State Backend --> Filesystem Backend --> Store %% Routing Logic Composite --> Routes{Routes} %% Connections from Routes Routes --> State Routes --> Filesystem Routes --> Store %% Styling style Routes fill:#333,stroke:#fff,stroke-width:2px

Specify a backend

You configure the backend when creating the deep agent. The filesystem middleware uses this backend for all tool operations.

# Default (StateBackend)
agent = create_deep_agent()

# Explicit backend instance
from deepagents.backends import FilesystemBackend
agent = create_deep_agent(backend=FilesystemBackend(root_dir="."))

Built-in Backends

StateBackend (ephemeral)

The default backend. Stores files in the LangGraph agent state for the current thread.

  • Scope: Persists across turns in the same thread (via checkpoints).
  • Use Case: Scratchpads, temporary files, intermediate results.
  • Feature: Automatic eviction of large tool outputs processing.
from deepagents.backends import StateBackend
# Factory function needed as it depends on runtime state
agent = create_deep_agent(backend=lambda rt: StateBackend(rt))

FilesystemBackend (local disk)

Reads and writes to the actual local disk. Use with caution.

  • Scope: Real filesystem access.
  • Use Case: Local coding assistants, CI/CD pipelines.
  • Security: use virtual_mode=True with root_dir to prevent directory traversal attacks.
from deepagents.backends import FilesystemBackend
agent = create_deep_agent(
    backend=FilesystemBackend(root_dir="./workspace", virtual_mode=True)
)

StoreBackend (LangGraph store)

Durable, cross-thread storage using LangGraph's BaseStore.

  • Scope: Persists across different conversations and threads.
  • Use Case: Long-term memory, user preferences, knowledge bases.
  • Namespace: Files are namespaced per assistant_id.
from deepagents.backends import StoreBackend
from langgraph.store.memory import InMemoryStore

agent = create_deep_agent(
    backend=lambda rt: StoreBackend(rt),
    store=InMemoryStore() # Required
)

Route to different backends

Use CompositeBackend to route file paths to different storage engines. Longest prefix wins.

from deepagents.backends import CompositeBackend, StateBackend, FilesystemBackend

def make_backend(runtime):
    return CompositeBackend(
        default=StateBackend(runtime), # Ephemeral for most things
        routes={
            "/memories/": FilesystemBackend(root_dir="/data/memories"),
            "/legacy/": FilesystemBackend(root_dir="/legacy_data")
        }
    )

agent = create_deep_agent(backend=make_backend)

Example Flow:

  • /workspace/plan.md → StateBackend (ephemeral)
  • /memories/user_prefs.txt → FilesystemBackend (persistent)

Use a virtual filesystem

You can implement custom backends by satisfying the BackendProtocol. This is useful for mapping abstract paths to databases (like S3 or SQL).

  • Paths: Absolute paths (/x/y.txt).
  • Listing: Implement ls_info and glob_info efficiently (e.g., using SQL LIKE).
  • Updates: External persistence should return files_update=None. Only in-state backends return a state update dict.

Add policy hooks

Wrap existing backends to enforce security policies, such as read-only paths or blocked directories.

from deepagents.backends.filesystem import FilesystemBackend
from deepagents.backends.protocol import WriteResult

class GuardedBackend(FilesystemBackend):
    def __init__(self, *, deny_prefixes: list[str], **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.deny_prefixes = deny_prefixes

    def write(self, file_path: str, content: str) -> WriteResult:
        if any(file_path.startswith(p) for p in self.deny_prefixes):
            return WriteResult(error=f"Writes are not allowed under {file_path}")
        return super().write(file_path, content)

Protocol reference

ls_info(path: str) -> list[FileInfo]

Return entries under the given path. Include is_dir, size, modified_at when available.

read(file_path: str, offset: int = 0, limit: int = 2000) -> str

Return text content. On missing file, return error string "Error: File '/x' not found".

write(file_path: str, content: str) -> WriteResult

Create or overwrite. External backends set files_update=None.

edit(file_path: str, old_string: str, new_string: str, replace_all: bool = False) -> EditResult

Locate old_string and replace with new_string. Enforce uniqueness unless replace_all=True.

glob_info(pattern: str, path: str = "/") -> list[FileInfo]

Return matched files as FileInfo entries.

grep_raw(pattern: str, ...) -> list[GrepMatch] | str

Return structured matches (path, line, text).
